prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: Safe epigenetic reset without loss of cell identity is an open problem, far from the Main KPI of 100,000,000 people with epigenetic resets. The first human partial-reprogramming trial, Life Biosciences ER-100 (OSK, doxycycline-inducible, injected locally in the eye for glaucoma and NAION), only had its IND cleared in January 2026 and is a phase 1 safety study in a handful of participants (https://longevity.technology/news/fda-clears-first-human-trial-of-epigenetic-reprogramming-therapy/). The 2025 review of in vivo reprogramming still lists teratoma formation, organ failure and loss of cell identity as unresolved, with identity loss demonstrated in pancreatic acinar cells and in transiently reprogrammed mesenchymal cells (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12610414/). Chemical reprogramming claimed to preserve identity is single-cell-line in vitro work with undisclosed cocktails (Yang et al., Aging 2023, https://static-site-aging-prod.impactaging.com/article/204896/pdf). No open protocol or open-source system for safe systemic reprogramming was found; published protocols are paper-bound and partly access-restricted.
